formulas.name: Betweenness (Freeman 1977)
formulas.where: Sum over ordered pairs \((s,t)\) with \(\sigma_{st}>0\). For an undirected graph each unordered pair is counted once, so the value is half of this sum. Pairs without a path are not terms of the sum.

formulas.name: Normalized betweenness
formulas.where: Divides by the number of pairs of other nodes, so the value lies in \([0,1]\) and is 1 for the centre of a star. Needs \(n\ge 3\).

formulas.name: Accumulation of dependencies (Brandes 2001)
formulas.where: Computes the same values as the first formula with one shortest-path search per source; the sum over \(s\) runs over ordered pairs, so an undirected graph's value is halved. Weighted graphs use Dijkstra's search with positive lengths.

variants.betweenness: The formulas above, for every node, with unit edge lengths unless weights are given as lengths.
variants.betweenness_approx: Same quantity, with the sum over sources \(s\) restricted to a random sample of size \(k\) and rescaled by \(n/k\); the value is an estimate, equal to the exact value when every node is a source.
variants.betweenness_simple: Same formula, tool-specific entry point (a call that returns the raw or simple version of the computation).
variants.cx_betweenness_subset: Sums over \(s\) in a source set \(S\) and \(t\) in a target set \(T\) only (Brandes 2008): \(\sum_{s\in S,t\in T}\sigma_{st}(v)/\sigma_{st}\); with \(S=T=V\) it is the formula above up to the pair-counting factor.

sum of distances \(\sum_{u\in R(v)}d(v,u)\) over the nodes \(v\) reaches

formulas.name: Closeness (Sabidussi 1966; Freeman 1978)
formulas.where: Inverse of the sum of distances to all other nodes; defined when every other node is reachable. Direction: distances out of \(v\) (out-closeness) or into \(v\) (in-closeness).

formulas.name: Normalized closeness
formulas.where: Inverse of the mean distance; 1 when \(v\) is adjacent to every other node. Needs \(n\ge 2\).

formulas.name: Reachable-nodes reading
formulas.where: Inverse of the mean distance to the nodes that \(v\) reaches; undefined (0/0) when \(r_v=0\).

formulas.name: Improved closeness (Wasserman and Faust 1994)
formulas.where: The reachable-nodes reading scaled by the fraction of nodes reached, so nodes that reach little score low; 0 when \(r_v=0\).

formulas.name: Residual closeness (Dangalchev 2006)
formulas.where: Nearby nodes dominate; unreachable nodes contribute 0.

formulas.name: Two-mode closeness (Borgatti and Everett 1997)
formulas.where: Normalized by the smallest possible distance sum of a node in a mode of size \(n_{\text{own}}\) with \(n_{\text{other}}\) nodes in the other mode: all other-mode nodes at distance 1 and the rest of its own mode at distance 2.

variants.closeness: The closeness formulas above; the tool's rule for unreachable nodes selects among the raw, reachable-nodes and improved forms, and the normalization selects the first or second.
variants.cat_closeness_incremental: Same closeness values, maintained by updating distances as edges are added instead of recomputing.
variants.cat_closeness_latora: Sum of inverse distances \(\sum_{u\ne v}1/d(v,u)\) (Latora and Marchiori 2001): the harmonic variant that stays defined on disconnected graphs.
variants.cat_closeness_newman_weighted: Closeness with minimum-total-weight paths, the weighted extension of the first formula as documented for the tool.
variants.cat_closeness_swan: Closeness computed in netrankr from a distance relation; its formula is not stated in the sources read.
variants.closeness_approx: Approximate, top-k and group closeness procedures of one tool: estimates by sampled pivots (with an error parameter), exact scores for the k best nodes, and group closeness.
variants.twomode:closeness: The two-mode formula: closeness normalized by the minimum possible distance sum for the node's mode.

salsa.note: The closed-form stationary distribution and the edge cases of the tool's implementation are not recorded in the sources read.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
in- and out-degree

formulas.name: SALSA authority chain (Lempel and Moran 2001)
formulas.where: Transition probability of a random walk on the authorities of the bipartite hub-authority graph: step back along an in-edge of \(i\) to a hub \(h\), then forward along one of \(h\)'s out-edges to \(j\). The authority scores are the stationary distribution of this chain; the hub chain is defined symmetrically.

variants.cat_salsa: SALSA hub or authority scores of one tool.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Nodes without in-edges are not authorities; nodes without out-edges are not hubs.
The stationary distribution is determined per connected component of the bipartite graph, weighted by the component's share.

formulas.name: Transformations of a distance relation
